solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Desire unknown nerd, a chocolate factory owner (5,5)

blocks.note: will = desire, as in 'against her will'
x, y and z are the algebraic unknowns
a wonk is a studious nerd, as in 'policy wonk'
used as it stands

annotation.surface: Someone yearns for an anonymous geek who happens to run a sweet factory.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'a' reads as part of the definition in the surface, but it is the final letter of the wordplay, so the definition starts at 'chocolate'.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by famous example: the eccentric proprietor in Roald Dahl's Charlie and the Chocolate Factory.

entries.clue: Restaurant employee drops one drink (5)

indicatorNotes.drops: the waiter lets a letter fall out of the word, like a plate slipping from a tray

blocks.note: the person who serves at table
one = I, the Roman numeral; this is the letter removed

annotation.surface: A clumsy waiter lets a customer's drink slip.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drops' reads as a waiter's accident with a glass; in the parse it means the Roman one falls out of the word.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain noun sense: the commonest thing anyone drinks, served free with every restaurant meal.

entries.clue: Fight to secure musical instruments (4,5)

blocks.note: to lock = to secure, as with a door
brass instruments such as the French horn

annotation.surface: Someone struggles to get hold of a set of musical instruments.
annotation.walkthrough: 'To' belongs to the wordplay, not a link: 'to secure' is the verb that gives the first word.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom from rutting stags, whose antlers tangle as they clash, used for any head-on quarrel.

entries.clue: Lout overturned dried grass on two ducks (5)

indicatorNotes.overturned: in a down clue, turning a word over flips it top to bottom, so it reads backwards
indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, the first piece sits on top of the second

blocks.note: hay is grass cut and dried for fodder
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, so O; two of them give a pair

annotation.surface: A yob tips over a hay bale onto a pair of ducks.
annotation.walkthrough: The ducks are not birds: a duck in cricket is a batter's score of zero, and crosswords turn zero into the letter O.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym with a literary root: the brutish human creatures in Gulliver's Travels gave the word for a coarse lout.

entries.clue: Resistance unit owes him money initially (3)

indicatorNotes.initially: at the start of each word, so take the opening letters

blocks.note: the opening letters of Owes, Him, Money

annotation.surface: A member of the resistance cell is in debt to a comrade.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Resistance unit' reads as a cell of rebels; it is the electrical sense.
annotation.definitionFit: A term from physics: the SI measure of how strongly a conductor opposes current, named after Georg Ohm.

entries.clue: King and a libertine admitting love for singing activity (7)

indicatorNotes.admitting: to admit is to let in, so the libertine lets the letter inside

blocks.note: K = king, as in chess notation
'and' just adds the A
a rake is a dissolute pleasure-seeker; it wraps around the next piece
love = nil in tennis, the shape of O

annotation.surface: A king and his dissolute companion let romance into their evening of song.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a royal party, which suits the answer; love is the tennis score, not romance.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain description: the Japanese pastime of singing along to recorded backing tracks.

entries.clue: Drinks bill extremely large in Arthur’s seat location? (5,5)

indicatorNotes.extremely: at the extremes, so take the first and last letters

blocks.note: a round is drinks bought for the whole group
a tab is a bar bill
the first and last letters of LargE

annotation.surface: A pub bill runs very high at Arthur's Seat, the hill in Edinburgh.
annotation.walkthrough: Arthur's Seat is a hill above Edinburgh, which the surface leans on; the question mark flags that the definition means King Arthur's place at his table.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic definition by wordplay on 'seat': King Arthur's knights sat around a table with no head, and his chair was at it.

entries.clue: Choose interesting course primarily related to vision (5)

indicatorNotes.primarily: in the first place, so take each word's opening letter

blocks.note: to opt = to choose
the opening letters of Interesting and Course

annotation.surface: Advice to a student to pick a stimulating class, apparently in ophthalmology.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Course' reads as a class to take; it only supplies its first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: An adjective from the Greek for sight, used in anatomy as in 'optic nerve'.

entries.clue: Continuous noise by bongo, say, is mediocre (7)

blocks.note: a steady low drone
a bongo is one kind of drum; 'say' marks the example

annotation.surface: A music critic grumbles that a droning bongo player is nothing special.
annotation.walkthrough: 'By' means next to, so the noise sits beside the instrument; the surface reads it as 'made by'.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: something dull and ordinary, with nothing to lift it above the average.

entries.clue: Time during intervention for relaxing exercise (10)

indicatorNotes.during: something that happens during an event falls within it, so the letter goes inside

blocks.note: T = time, as in physics formulas
mediation is stepping in to settle a dispute; it holds the letter

annotation.surface: A timeout during a tense negotiation to calm everyone down.
annotation.walkthrough: The two words differ by a single letter, which goes in after the fourth, so the container is easy to miss.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by function: a practice of focused stillness done to calm the mind.

entries.clue: Somehow help Ron to the top of the world? (5,4)

indicatorNotes.Somehow: the letters get there by some unspecified rearrangement

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: A plea to assist Ron's climb to the summit of the world.
annotation.walkthrough: 'To' looks like a link to the definition, but it is part of the fodder: the first two words alone are two letters short.
annotation.definitionFit: A playful definition, hence the question mark: maps put north at the top, so the pole is literally uppermost.

entries.clue: Dear old partner lost in thought (9)

blocks.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner
deep in reflection

annotation.surface: Someone's beloved former partner sits deep in reflection.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dear' looks like an affectionate address to the old partner; it is the price sense.
annotation.definitionFit: A second sense of 'dear': high in price, as in 'petrol is dear'.

entries.clue: Not even unusual? (3)

blocks.note: the arithmetic sense: a number that does not divide by two
the everyday sense: strange

annotation.surface: Someone wonders whether a thing is not even out of the ordinary.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'even' as an intensifier ('not even unusual'); in the parse it is the number sense.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses of one word: numbers like 3 and 7 are not even, and a peculiar thing is unusual.

entries.clue: Vet ran dodgy inn (6)

indicatorNotes.dodgy: something dodgy is not quite straight, so the letters are out of order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 6 letters

annotation.surface: An animal doctor was running a disreputable pub on the side.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dodgy' belongs with 'inn' in the surface but is the anagram signal working on the first two words.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an old-fashioned word for a place selling drink and often lodging.

entries.clue: Country house contains an orchid (7)

indicatorNotes.contains: the house holds the other piece inside it

blocks.note: a villa is a large country residence; it holds the next piece
used as it stands

annotation.surface: A stately home has an orchid growing in it.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'an' reads as the article before 'orchid', but it is the piece inside the house.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by genus: the flavouring comes from the pods of a climbing tropical orchid.

entries.clue: Positive pub tea is awful (6)

indicatorNotes.is awful: letters in an awful state are a mess, so rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 6 letters

annotation.surface: An optimist's review of the tea served in a pub turns out damning.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface contradicts itself, 'positive' then 'awful'; that clash is the setter hiding the definition at the front.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym for a cheerful, optimistic mood, borrowed from the lifted beat in music.

entries.clue: Outlaw’s gang incomplete (3)

indicatorNotes.incomplete: a word left incomplete is missing its final letter

blocks.note: a gang of robbers or musicians, a group; its last letter goes

annotation.surface: An outlaw's gang is short of members.
annotation.walkthrough: The apostrophe stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay; 'Outlaw' is the verb, not the bandit.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb synonym: to outlaw something is to prohibit it by law.

entries.clue: Rigid loop found in small shelter (9)

indicatorNotes.found in: the loop is located inside the shelter

blocks.note: S = small, the clothing-size abbreviation
a canvas shelter; the loop goes inside it
a ring is a closed loop

annotation.surface: A stiff loop of rope turns up inside a little tent.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Small shelter' reads as one idea, a little tent, but it is two pieces, and the loop goes into the second after its first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym used of rules and standards: strict and unbending.

entries.clue: Beatle starts to needle George in Brazilian city (5)

indicatorNotes.starts to: the starts of the next words, so take their opening letters
indicatorNotes.in: those letters go inside the city

blocks.note: Rio de Janeiro; it holds the two letters
the opening letters of Needle and George

annotation.surface: A Beatle begins to tease George Harrison on a trip to Brazil.
annotation.walkthrough: George is not the Beatle here; he only supplies a G, and the answer is his bandmate.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Beatles' drummer, Ringo Starr, known by his first name.

entries.clue: Polished off and defeated without leader (5)

indicatorNotes.without leader: a word without its leader has lost the letter at its head

blocks.note: beaten = defeated; its first letter goes

annotation.surface: A team finished off and beaten after losing its captain.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Polished off' reads as defeat in the surface, but it is the eating sense, as in finishing a plate.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal idiom: food polished off has been finished entirely, consumed.

entries.clue: Spice up some rotten live news (7)

indicatorNotes.some: only some of the following letters are used

blocks.note: the answer sits inside rotTEN LIVE News

annotation.surface: Adding a bit of drama to a bad live news broadcast.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Some' reads as 'a bit of' news; it tells you to take part of the letters, which run across three words.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb synonym: to spice something up is to make it livelier and more exciting.

entries.clue: Regularly avoided struggle (3)

indicatorNotes.Regularly: take letters at regular intervals, every other one

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of aVoIdEd

annotation.surface: Someone habitually sidestepped a fight.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' reads as 'often'; it means every other letter, starting from the second.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb synonym: to vie is to strive against a rival for something.

entries.clue: Keen on covering footballer’s last start (5)

indicatorNotes.covering: a cover wraps over something, so the outer word goes around the letter
indicatorNotes.last: the footballer's last is the final letter of that word

blocks.note: to be into something is to be keen on it; it wraps the letter
the final letter of footballeR

annotation.surface: A fan is excited about a player's most recent first-team appearance.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Start' reads as a footballer's appearance in the team; it is the opening of a piece of music or writing.
annotation.definitionFit: A short informal form of 'introduction', the opening section of a song or text.

entries.clue: Trade Monet works for art gallery (4,6)

indicatorNotes.works: the letters are worked into a new shape

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters

annotation.surface: A dealer offers Monet's paintings to a gallery.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Works' reads as paintings, which fits Monet; it is the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: London's national museum of modern art, in a former power station on the Thames.
